<issue identifier="MM-480">
<title>Create flow: approve OAuth consent in-wallet, without a browser takeover or password prompt</title>
<description>
Extends <issue id="9cfb3005-9011-4b73-bf18-43ecacfd64ce" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-441/wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent-phase-a-pending-authorization-primitive">MM-441</issue>/<issue id="16b372c8-06fa-4a9b-b6c7-239e5b4455e9" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-442/wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent-phase-b-qr-scan-on-the-consent-page">MM-442</issue> (wallet-confirmed OAuth consent) and resolves the open question left in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-18-wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent.md`:

> **Does the wallet-path consent page still render the password form?** Proposal: render the password form only for accounts that have one (requires the identifier first...)

## Observed

At the end of account creation the wallet advances to `authenticating`, which calls `startOAuthFlow(handle)` (`AuthenticatingScreen.svelte`) and opens the authorize page as a full-screen takeover over the app. The page offers two paths, and for a freshly created passwordless account **neither is reachable**:

* **Password form** — the account has no password.
* **Wallet path** — the instructions are "scan this with Obsign on your phone" and "open Obsign and enter this code". Both assume the browser is somewhere other than Obsign. Here the browser is a modal owned by Obsign, so the handoff points at the app hosting it, and dismissing the modal cancels the OAuth flow.

Signup therefore cannot complete on a passwordless account. This is the gate on shipping `accounts.password_optional` to a public beta.

## Why the obvious fix is unsafe

Hiding the password form for accounts that lack one requires knowing the account at render time. It isn't known: `oauth_authorize.rs` (~line 485) deliberately leaves `account_did` NULL because the client-supplied `login_hint` is unverified. Branching the rendered page on whether an account has a password makes `GET /oauth/authorize` an unauthenticated account-existence and credential-shape oracle — the property `delete_account.rs:37` explicitly preserves elsewhere. The design plan's "requires the identifier first" parenthetical is this problem, unsolved.

## Proposed shape

Two independent changes; the first is the fix, the second is general polish.

### 1. Same-device, no-browser consent for wallet-initiated authorization (the fix)

The wallet has just authored the genesis op with the device key and holds a fresh session — round-tripping through a web consent page to prove an identity it demonstrably possesses is ceremony with no security value, and the takeover makes it unreachable regardless.

The approval machinery already exists: `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id` and `confirm_oauth_consent` (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/oauth_consent.rs`). The only gap is that `request_id` is minted as a side effect of rendering HTML (`create_pending_request`, called from the `GET /oauth/authorize` handler).

* Add a JSON affordance so a wallet-native client can create the pending authorization directly and receive `{request_id, user_code}` without rendering a consent page.
* Create flow then runs entirely in-process: mint request → preview → biometric gate → sign envelope → confirm → complete → receive the authorization code. No web view, no takeover, no password form.
* The identity is already registered in IdentityStore before this point (`finishCreateFlow` → `registerCreatedIdentity`, `apps/identity-wallet/src/routes/+page.svelte:543`, ahead of `step = 'complete'`), so the wallet has a signable identity to approve with.

**Check first:** what the post-create OAuth is actually for. `perform_did_ceremony` already persists a session token to the Keychain. If that session covers what the app does next, the create flow may not need an OAuth round trip at all and this collapses to deleting a step.

### 2. Client-declared wallet-native rendering (general)

For wallet-initiated authorizations that *do* render a page, let the wallet's canonical OAuth client (`identitywallet.obsign.org`) signal that only the wallet path should be rendered. Keying off `client_id` reveals nothing about any account — the client declares its own capability — so it carries none of the oracle risk of keying off `login_hint`.

## Acceptance criteria

* A passwordless account created in the wallet reaches the home screen without a browser takeover and without ever being shown a password field.
* No consent-page rendering decision depends on `login_hint` or on whether a given account has a password; `GET /oauth/authorize` remains non-enumerable.
* The in-process approval reuses the existing signed-envelope verification (binding `request_id`, `client_id`, granted-scope hash) — no second, weaker approval path.
* Scope reduction stays available on the in-wallet path.
* Cross-device and typed-code paths are unchanged and still work for third-party clients.
* Drivable end to end in the browser harness (`VITE_HARNESS=fake`), including the passwordless create path.
</description>

<id>ff3e493f-009c-4211-b4de-4ed9a2e7d1a4</id>
<title>Passwordless auth: retire the account password in favor of device-key/passkey factors</title>
<description>
Follow-up to the passwordless design exploration captured in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-12-passwordless-auth.md` (branch `claude/passwordless-login-bc4umw`).

## Why

The password is already a second-class credential in this architecture: the wallet logs in via OAuth+DPoP and retains no password, the root of trust is the Secure-Enclave device key holding `rotationKeys[0]`, `accounts.password_hash` has been nullable since V008, and `createSession` already falls through to app-password verification for accounts with a NULL main password. Meanwhile password reset is dead in practice (outbound email is stubbed, <issue id="fbeb902e-c32b-400a-af47-37eccd58d65b" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-211/outbound-email-delivery-email-confirmationupdate-endpoints">MM-211</issue>), so the password is an unrecoverable liability posing as a recovery factor. Identity recovery never depended on it — that's the device key's 2-of-3 Shamir split.

## What the password still gates (the actual work)

1. **OAuth consent** (`oauth_authorize.rs`) — the wallet's own login path; a NULL-hash account cannot pass consent today. Needs a device-key-signed or passkey (WebAuthn) factor. The signed-envelope verification pattern already exists for admin-companion devices (`auth/guards.rs::verify_admin_device_request`).
2. **Account creation** — non-empty password required in `/v1/dids` and `createAccount` new-account mode; make optional (migration mode already stores NULL).
3. `deleteAccount` — password + email token in body; rework to email-token-or-wallet-signature for passwordless accounts.
4. Third-party clients (Bluesky app, goat) keep working via **app passwords** minted in the wallet — zero server changes needed.

## Phasing (from the design plan)

* **Phase 1:** optional password at creation; device-key/passkey factor on OAuth consent; `deleteAccount` rework. Keep interop endpoints (password branch of `createSession`, standard `createAccount`) for migrated-in accounts.
* **Phase 2:** cross-device login approval — QR-scan (wallet-initiated, phishing-resistant) first; **push-to-approve** later, once the E2E-encrypted notification relay lands (<pull-request id="34230e45-6259-4c9a-b58d-6b135adf84e3" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/review/design-exploration-e2e-encrypted-notification-relay-for-self-hosted-327f880332d1">malpercio-dev/ezpds#207</pull-request>, `docs/design-plans/2026-07-10-notification-relay.md`). Push-approve needs MFA-fatigue mitigations (origin display, number matching).
* **Hard prerequisite (parallel):** the Shamir reconstruction ceremony (or iCloud-synced passkeys), so a lost device is not a total PDS lockout before the password escape hatch is removed.

## Definition of done (exploration → plan promotion)

* Full design plan with acceptance criteria promoted from the exploration doc
* Decision recorded: passkey/WebAuthn vs device-key-signed consent as the primary factor
* Recovery-ceremony dependency scheduled ahead of any password removal
</description>
</parent-issue>

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/linear-workflow

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

{"id":"MM-480","title":"Create flow: approve OAuth consent in-wallet, without a browser takeover or password prompt","description":"Extends <issue id="9cfb3005-9011-4b73-bf18-43ecacfd64ce" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-441/wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent-phase-a-pending-authorization-primitive">MM-441</issue>/<issue id="16b372c8-06fa-4a9b-b6c7-239e5b4455e9" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-442/wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent-phase-b-qr-scan-on-the-consent-page">MM-442</issue> (wallet-confirmed OAuth consent) and resolves the open question left in `docs/design-plans/2026-07-18-wallet-confirmed-oauth-consent.md`:

> **Does the wallet-path consent page still render the password form?** Proposal: render the password form only for accounts that have one (requires the identifier first...)

## Observed

At the end of account creation the wallet advances to `authenticating`, which calls `startOAuthFlow(handle)` (`AuthenticatingScreen.svelte`) and opens the authorize page as a full-screen takeover over the app. The page offers two paths, and for a freshly created passwordless account **neither is reachable**:

* **Password form** — the account has no password.
* **Wallet path** — the instructions are "scan this with Obsign on your phone" and "open Obsign and enter this code". Both assume the browser is somewhere other than Obsign. Here the browser is a modal owned by Obsign, so the handoff points at the app hosting it, and dismissing the modal cancels the OAuth flow.

Signup therefore cannot complete on a passwordless account. This is the gate on shipping `accounts.password_optional` to a public beta.

## Why the obvious fix is unsafe

Hiding the password form for accounts that lack one requires knowing the account at render time. It isn't known: `oauth_authorize.rs` (~line 485) deliberately leaves `account_did` NULL because the client-supplied `login_hint` is unverified. Branching the rendered page on whether an account has a password makes `GET /oauth/authorize` an unauthenticated account-existence and credential-shape oracle — the property `delete_account.rs:37` explicitly preserves elsewhere. The design plan's "requires the identifier first" parenthetical is this problem, unsolved.

## Proposed shape

Two independent changes; the first is the fix, the second is general polish.

### 1. Same-device, no-browser consent for wallet-initiated authorization (the fix)

The wallet has just authored the genesis op with the device key and holds a fresh session — round-tripping through a web consent page to prove an identity it demonstrably possesses is ceremony with no security value, and the takeover makes it unreachable regardless.

The approval machinery already exists: `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id` and `confirm_oauth_consent` (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/oauth_consent.rs`). The only gap is that `request_id` is minted as a side effect of rendering HTML (`create_pending_request`, called from the `GET /oauth/authorize` handler).

* Add a JSON affordance so a wallet-native client can create the pending authorization directly and receive `{request_id, user_code}` without rendering a consent page.
* Create flow then runs entirely in-process: mint request → preview → biometric gate → sign envelope → confirm → complete → receive the authorization code. No web view, no takeover, no password form.
* The identity is already registered in IdentityStore before this point (`finishCreateFlow` → `registerCreatedIdentity`, `apps/identity-wallet/src/routes/+page.svelte:543`, ahead of `step = 'complete'`), so the wallet has a signable identity to approve with.

**Check first:** what the post-create OAuth is actually for. `perform_did_ceremony` already persists a session token to the Keychain. If that session covers what the app does next, the create flow may not need an OAuth round trip at all and this collapses to deleting a step.

### 2. Client-declared wallet-native rendering (general)

For wallet-initiated authorizations that *do* render a page, let the wallet's canonical OAuth client (`identitywallet.obsign.org`) signal that only the wallet path should be rendered. Keying off `client_id` reveals nothing about any account — the client declares its own capability — so it carries none of the oracle risk of keying off `login_hint`.

## Acceptance criteria

* A passwordless account created in the wallet reaches the home screen without a browser takeover and without ever being shown a password field.
* No consent-page rendering decision depends on `login_hint` or on whether a given account has a password; `GET /oauth/authorize` remains non-enumerable.
* The in-process approval reuses the existing signed-envelope verification (binding `request_id`, `client_id`, granted-scope hash) — no second, weaker approval path.
* Scope reduction stays available on the in-wallet path.
* Cross-device and typed-code paths are unchanged and still work for third-party clients.

The approval machinery already exists: `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id` and `confirm_oauth_consent` (`apps/identity-wallet/src-tauri/src/oauth_consent.rs`). The only gap is that `request_id` is minted as a side effect of rendering HTML (`create_pending_request`, called from the `GET /oauth/authorize` handler).

* Add a JSON affordance so a wallet-native client can create the pending authorization directly and receive `{request_id, user_code}` without rendering a consent page.
* Create flow then runs entirely in-process: mint request → preview → biometric gate → sign envelope → confirm → complete → receive the authorization code. No web view, no takeover, no password form.
* The identity is already registered in IdentityStore before this point (`finishCreateFlow` → `registerCreatedIdentity`, `apps/identity-wallet/src/routes/+page.svelte:543`, ahead of `step = 'complete'`), so the wallet has a signable identity to approve with.

**Check first:** what the post-create OAuth is actually for. `perform_did_ceremony` already persists a session token to the Keychain. If that session covers what the app does next, the create flow may not need an OAuth round trip at all and this collapses to deleting a step.

### 2. Client-declared wallet-native rendering (general)

For wallet-initiated authorizations that *do* render a page, let the wallet's canonical OAuth client (`identitywallet.obsign.org`) signal that only the wallet path should be rendered. Keying off `client_id` reveals nothing about any account — the client declares its own capability — so it carries none of the oracle risk of keying off `login_hint`.

## Acceptance criteria

* A passwordless account created in the wallet reaches the home screen without a browser takeover and without ever being shown a password field.
* No consent-page rendering decision depends on `login_hint` or on whether a given account has a password; `GET /oauth/authorize` remains non-enumerable.
* The in-process approval reuses the existing signed-envelope verification (binding `request_id`, `client_id`, granted-scope hash) — no second, weaker approval path.
* Scope reduction stays available on the in-wallet path.
* Cross-device and typed-code paths are unchanged and still work for third-party clients.

1	# Wallet-Confirmed OAuth Consent (Passwordless Sign-In to OAuth Apps)
2	
3	Status: **design exploration** — extends the passwordless-auth exploration
4	([2026-07-12-passwordless-auth.md](2026-07-12-passwordless-auth.md), MM-312) by deciding
5	the concrete cross-device mechanism it left open: device-code entry (Netflix-style) vs
6	number matching (GitHub-style) vs QR vs push. Captures the discussion of 2026-07-18.
7	Implementation tracked as sub-issues of MM-312:
8	[MM-441](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-441) (Phase A),
9	[MM-442](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-442) (Phase B),
10	[MM-443](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-443) (Phase C).
11	
12	## Problem
13	
14	A sovereign account cannot sign in to OAuth apps at all. The consent handler maps a NULL
15	or empty `password_hash` unconditionally to `WrongPassword`
16	(`crates/pds/src/routes/oauth_authorize.rs:560-564`, covered by
17	`post_approve_with_mobile_account_rerenders_consent_page`), and wallet-created /
18	migrated-in accounts store NULL by design (MM-306). So the account that *most* embodies
19	the product's identity model is the one locked out of the ATProto OAuth app ecosystem.
20	There is no push infrastructure yet, but the design must leave a clean slot for it
21	(notification relay, MM-311).
22	
23	## The framing: one primitive, several channels
24	
25	"Device code vs number matching" is not an architecture choice — it is a choice of
26	**discovery channel** onto a single server-side primitive. Decide the primitive once, and
27	every channel (typed code, same-device handoff, QR, push) becomes a thin variant:
28	
29	> **Pending authorization request** — created by the consent page in place of the
30	> password check; approved out-of-band by the wallet with a device-key-signed envelope;
31	> observed by the consent page until it can complete the normal redirect.
32	
33	Nearly all of this already exists in the tree:
34	
35	| Piece | Existing machinery |
36	|---|---|
37	| Pending-request state machine + "approved elsewhere" polling | agent claim ceremony: `agent_claim_attempts` (V037/V038), `routes/oauth_token/claim_polling.rs` (`authorization_pending` / `slow_down` / success, poll throttling, race re-read) |
38	| Passwordless approval credential | sovereign session: `routes/sovereign_session.rs` — canonical envelope signed by a key in the account's **authoritative PLC `rotationKeys`**, nonce anti-replay, timestamp window |
39	| Canonical signed-envelope pattern | ADR-0018 admin envelope (`auth/guards.rs::verify_admin_device_request`, `apps/admin-companion/src-tauri/src/signing.rs`) |
40	| Wallet approval UX (enter code → preview grants → biometric → confirm) | `AgentClaimApprovalScreen.svelte` + `agents.rs` IPC (claim-preview / claim-confirm) |
41	| Consent page + per-scope checkboxes | `oauth_templates.rs::render_consent_page`, MM-237 scope reduction |
42	| Push envelope for a future `login-approval` type | notification relay design ([2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](2026-07-10-notification-relay.md)) already names `{type: "login-approval", request_id, client_name, origin, code}` |
43	
44	The genuinely new pieces are one table, one approval route, one status route, a second
45	path through `oauth_authorize.rs`, and one wallet screen variant.
46	
47	## Channel analysis
48	
49	The security-relevant property is **who carries the binding between the login surface and
50	the wallet**:
51	
52	- **Wallet-initiated** channels (user types a code from the page into the wallet, taps a
53	  link on the page, or scans the page's QR): the *user* carries the binding from the
54	  thing they are logging into. Blind approval is impossible — the wallet has nothing to
55	  show until the user brings it a request.
56	- **Wallet-notified** channels (push, or the wallet polling for pending requests): the
57	  request finds the user. This is where MFA-fatigue / blind-tap attacks live, and where
58	  **number matching** earns its keep — it forces the approver to prove they can see the
59	  login surface.
60	
61	| Channel | Needs push? | Same-device? | Camera? | Phishing profile |
62	|---|---|---|---|---|
63	| Typed short code (Netflix) | no | yes (clunky but works) | no | RFC 8628-style code phishing: attacker starts a login, socially engineers the victim into entering the attacker's code. Mitigated by the wallet preview (client, origin, scopes) before biometric confirm |
64	| Same-device handoff (link on consent page opens wallet with `request_id`) | no | **the** same-device answer | no | same as typed code, minus transcription |
65	| QR scan (page shows QR of `request_id` + origin) | no | no (can't scan own screen) | yes | strongest cross-device: user starts from the page, no transcription, wallet verifies origin from the request server-side |
66	| Push + number match (GitHub/MS Authenticator) | **yes** (MM-311) | yes | no | blind-tap risk is the failure mode; number matching + origin display are the standard mitigations |
67	
68	Two observations that settle the ordering:
69	
70	1. **Number matching is a mitigation for the push channel, not an alternative to the
71	   code.** In every wallet-initiated channel it is redundant — the user already carried
72	   the binding. Building GitHub-style matching *without* push would require the wallet to
73	   discover pending requests by polling, which in turn requires the consent page to
74	   pre-bind a typed handle to the request. That creates an unauthenticated surface where
75	   anyone typing a victim's handle at any Custos consent page makes a prompt appear in
76	   the victim's wallet — importing the MFA-fatigue problem *before* gaining push's
77	   convenience. Rejected as a v1.
78	2. **Same-device is the common case for a mobile-only PDS** (the OAuth client app is on
79	   the same phone as the wallet), and it is exactly the case QR cannot serve. The typed
80	   code always works as the universal fallback (no camera, no push, accessibility-safe,
81	   cross-device and same-device alike) — which is why it ships first.
82	
83	## Shape
84	
85	### The pending request
86	
87	New table (name illustrative) `pending_oauth_authorizations`:
88	
89	- `request_id` (random, high-entropy — used in QR / handoff link / push payload)
90	- `user_code` (short, human-typeable, e.g. 8 chars grouped — the Netflix path; formatted
91	  distinctly from the agent claim code and the operator claim code; ADR-0026 already
92	  warns these "share a word, not a mechanism")
93	- client_id + resolved client metadata snapshot, requested scopes, PAR linkage
94	- requesting origin/IP/user-agent (for wallet display)
95	- optional `login_hint` DID (pre-bound account, if the client supplied one)
96	- status: `pending` / `approved` / `denied` / `expired`; granted-scope set on approval
97	- created/expires (~5 min), single-use
98	
99	### Consent-page flow (`oauth_authorize.rs`, second path)
100	
101	1. `GET /oauth/authorize` for a passwordless-capable flow renders the wallet path
102	   (alongside the password form while passworded accounts exist): creates the pending
103	   request, shows the `user_code`, an "Open in Obsign" handoff link carrying
104	   `request_id` (Phase A), and later a QR (Phase B).
105	2. The page observes `GET /oauth/authorize/status?request_id=…` (JS poll with the same
106	   `slow_down` throttling discipline as `claim_polling.rs`; no-JS fallback: an
107	   "I've approved — continue" button).
108	3. On `approved`, the page completes through the **existing** tail of
109	   `post_authorization`: scope reduction already decided, `store_authorization_code`,
110	   303 to `redirect_uri?code=…&state=…&iss=…`. The token endpoint (PKCE + DPoP) is
111	   untouched.
112	
113	### Wallet approval
114	
115	Reuses the agent-claim screen shape: enter code (or arrive via handoff/QR/push with
116	`request_id`) → **preview** (client name, origin, requesting IP/geo, scope list —
117	reusing the scope-preview treatment from `AgentClaimApprovalScreen.svelte`, and the
118	per-scope uncheck moves here: the wallet is the trusted UI for this path, so the granted
119	set is chosen in the wallet, not on the page) → biometric gate → sign → submit.
120	
121	Approval credential: a **device-key-signed canonical envelope** in the
122	`sovereign_session.rs` mold — domain-versioned string binding server DID, account DID,
123	signing key, `request_id`, `client_id`, a hash of the granted scope set, timestamp,
124	nonce; verified against the **authoritative current PLC `rotationKeys`** (same
125	authoritative-fetch discipline, same nonce anti-replay pattern). This keeps consent
126	strictly key-sovereign: the thing that can approve a login is the thing that owns the
127	identity, sessions optional. (The alternative — authenticate the approval route with
128	`authenticate_account_owner` and skip the envelope — is less code but binds approval to
129	session state instead of the key; the envelope also gives per-approval non-repudiation
130	for the audit log.) Passkeys/WebAuthn remain the complementary *browser-native* factor
131	from the MM-312 open question — additive later, not a competitor to this path.
132	
133	Account binding: if the request carries a `login_hint`, the approving wallet's DID must
134	match. Otherwise the approving wallet binds its DID at approval time (exactly like the
135	agent claim confirm), and the wallet screen states it explicitly: "Sign in to
136	**{client}** at **{origin}** as **@{handle}**".
137	
138	### The push slot (Phase C, after MM-311)
139	
140	Push adds only a delivery path: Custos seals `{type: "login-approval", request_id,
141	client_name, origin, code}` to the device (the relay design's exact payload), the wallet
142	deep-links into the same approval screen — with **number matching now mandatory**: the
143	consent page displays a 2-digit number for push-delivered prompts and the wallet requires
144	the user to enter/select it before the biometric gate, plus origin display. Nothing about
145	the primitive, the envelope, or the completion path changes.
146	
147	## Suggested phasing
148	
149	- **Phase A — code + handoff (no push, no camera).** The pending-request table/routes,
150	  the second consent-page path, typed `user_code` entry in the wallet (clone of the
151	  agent-claim screen), the same-device handoff link. Depends on nothing unbuilt.
152	  **Landed (2026-07-18):** `pending_oauth_authorizations` + `oauth_consent_audit_events`
153	  (V056), `crypto::encode_oauth_consent_envelope` (+ shared golden vector), the
154	  `routes/oauth_consent.rs` routes (wallet preview, `slow_down`-throttled status poll,
155	  device-key-signed approve/deny against authoritative PLC `rotationKeys`, browser
156	  completion through the existing code-issuance tail), the wallet path on the consent page,
157	  and the wallet's `oauth_consent.rs` IPC + `OAuthConsentApprovalScreen`. The signed
158	  envelope binds `request_id` + `client_id` + decision + granted-scope hash; single-use is
159	  enforced by the guarded status transitions (which, with the `request_id` binding, subsume
160	  a nonce store — no separate nonce table). Handoff link degrades to copy-the-code (the
161	  wallet has no deep-link handler yet, per ADR-0006).
162	- **Phase B — QR.** Encode `request_id` + origin on the consent page; wallet scan screen
163	  feeding the same approval flow. Camera plumbing is the only new work.
164	  **Landed (2026-07-19):** the consent page renders an inline-SVG QR (`qrcodegen` →
165	  `render_qr_svg` in `oauth_templates.rs`) encoding the wallet's private-use handoff URI
166	  (`org.obsign.identitywallet:/consent?request_id=…&origin=…`) beside the typed `user_code`, which
167	  stays rendered as the no-camera / accessibility fallback; the same URI backs both the QR and the
168	  same-device "Open in Obsign" link. The wallet gains a `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id` IPC
169	  command (the server's preview endpoint already resolved by `request_id`) and a camera scan screen
170	  on `OAuthConsentApprovalScreen` via `@tauri-apps/plugin-barcode-scanner` (mobile-only, `#[cfg(mobile)]`,
171	  `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `barcode-scanner:default`). The scan path extracts **only** the
172	  `request_id` from the QR (`parseConsentQr`) and re-verifies it server-side — the client/origin/scope
173	  the wallet displays always come from the server's record, never the QR — then feeds the identical
174	  preview → biometric → device-key-signed-envelope flow. No server protocol change beyond encoding
175	  the QR payload.
176	- **Phase C — push + number matching.** After the notification relay (MM-311) lands:
177	  `login-approval` notification type, deep-link approve/deny, number-match UX.
178	
179	Prerequisite note: the 2026-07-12 exploration named the Shamir **reconstruction**
180	ceremony a hard prerequisite for removing the password escape hatch; both reconstruction
181	ceremonies (escrow-assisted and sovereign) have since landed (`share_recovery.rs`;
182	[identity-and-key-custody.md](../architecture/identity-and-key-custody.md), verified
183	2026-07-18), so that gate is satisfied.
184	
185	## Security invariants (all channels)
186	
187	- Wallet approval screen always shows client name, origin/redirect host, requested
188	  scopes, and requesting IP/geo before the biometric gate; approval is impossible
189	  without the preview render.
190	- `user_code`/`request_id` single-use, ~5-minute expiry, rate-limited creation per
191	  client and per IP; status endpoint throttled like `claim_polling.rs`.
192	- The signed envelope binds the specific request (`request_id`, `client_id`, granted
193	  scope hash) — an approval cannot be replayed onto a different request or a widened
194	  scope set.
195	- Approval verification consults authoritative PLC state, never the cached DID doc
196	  (matching `sovereign_session.rs`).
197	- Denials and approvals both terminate the request; audit rows in the mold of
198	  `agent_audit`.
199	
200	## Open questions
201	
202	- **Same-device handoff mechanics on iOS.** ADR-0006 established that *server-initiated*
203	  redirects cannot launch the wallet from a browser context; a *user-tapped* universal
204	  link from inside another app's `ASWebAuthenticationSession`/`SFSafariViewController`
205	  is a different case but needs on-device validation. The typed code is the guaranteed
206	  fallback either way, so this only gates polish, not the phase.
207	- **Return-trip UX after same-device approval**: the user must app-switch back to the
208	  client app whose consent page then completes — acceptable (this is how bank-app
209	  confirmation flows feel) but worth prototyping.
210	- **Does the wallet-path consent page still render the password form?** Proposal:
211	  render the password form only for accounts that have one (requires the identifier
212	  first, or render both paths side by side as today's form does with checkboxes).
213	- **Number format for the Phase C match code**: 2-digit select-from-three (Microsoft
214	  style) vs type-the-number (GitHub style). Type-the-number is stronger against
215	  guess-taps; decide with the push UX.
216

migrated-in accounts store NULL by design (MM-306). So the account that *most* embodies
the product's identity model is the one locked out of the ATProto OAuth app ecosystem.
There is no push infrastructure yet, but the design must leave a clean slot for it
(notification relay, MM-311).

## The framing: one primitive, several channels

"Device code vs number matching" is not an architecture choice — it is a choice of
**discovery channel** onto a single server-side primitive. Decide the primitive once, and
every channel (typed code, same-device handoff, QR, push) becomes a thin variant:

> **Pending authorization request** — created by the consent page in place of the
> password check; approved out-of-band by the wallet with a device-key-signed envelope;
> observed by the consent page until it can complete the normal redirect.

Nearly all of this already exists in the tree:

| Piece | Existing machinery |
|---|---|
| Pending-request state machine + "approved elsewhere" polling | agent claim ceremony: `agent_claim_attempts` (V037/V038), `routes/oauth_token/claim_polling.rs` (`authorization_pending` / `slow_down` / success, poll throttling, race re-read) |
| Passwordless approval credential | sovereign session: `routes/sovereign_session.rs` — canonical envelope signed by a key in the account's **authoritative PLC `rotationKeys`**, nonce anti-replay, timestamp window |
| Canonical signed-envelope pattern | ADR-0018 admin envelope (`auth/guards.rs::verify_admin_device_request`, `apps/admin-companion/src-tauri/src/signing.rs`) |
| Wallet approval UX (enter code → preview grants → biometric → confirm) | `AgentClaimApprovalScreen.svelte` + `agents.rs` IPC (claim-preview / claim-confirm) |
| Consent page + per-scope checkboxes | `oauth_templates.rs::render_consent_page`, MM-237 scope reduction |
| Push envelope for a future `login-approval` type | notification relay design ([2026-07-10-notification-relay.md](2026-07-10-notification-relay.md)) already names `{type: "login-approval", request_id, client_name, origin, code}` |

The genuinely new pieces are one table, one approval route, one status route, a second
path through `oauth_authorize.rs`, and one wallet screen variant.

## Channel analysis

The security-relevant property is **who carries the binding between the login surface and
the wallet**:

- **Wallet-initiated** channels (user types a code from the page into the wallet, taps a
  link on the page, or scans the page's QR): the *user* carries the binding from the
  thing they are logging into. Blind approval is impossible — the wallet has nothing to
  show until the user brings it a request.
- **Wallet-notified** channels (push, or the wallet polling for pending requests): the
  request finds the user. This is where MFA-fatigue / blind-tap attacks live, and where
  **number matching** earns its keep — it forces the approver to prove they can see the
  login surface.

| Channel | Needs push? | Same-device? | Camera? | Phishing profile |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Typed short code (Netflix) | no | yes (clunky but works) | no | RFC 8628-style code phishing: attacker starts a login, socially engineers the victim into entering the attacker's code. Mitigated by the wallet preview (client, origin, scopes) before biometric confirm |
| Same-device handoff (link on consent page opens wallet with `request_id`) | no | **the** same-device answer | no | same as typed code, minus transcription |
| QR scan (page shows QR of `request_id` + origin) | no | no (can't scan own screen) | yes | strongest cross-device: user starts from the page, no transcription, wallet verifies origin from the request server-side |
| Push + number match (GitHub/MS Authenticator) | **yes** (MM-311) | yes | no | blind-tap risk is the failure mode; number matching + origin display are the standard mitigations |

Two observations that settle the ordering:

1. **Number matching is a mitigation for the push channel, not an alternative to the
   code.** In every wallet-initiated channel it is redundant — the user already carried
   the binding. Building GitHub-style matching *without* push would require the wallet to
   discover pending requests by polling, which in turn requires the consent page to
   pre-bind a typed handle to the request. That creates an unauthenticated surface where
   anyone typing a victim's handle at any Custos consent page makes a prompt appear in
   the victim's wallet — importing the MFA-fatigue problem *before* gaining push's
   convenience. Rejected as a v1.
2. **Same-device is the common case for a mobile-only PDS** (the OAuth client app is on
   the same phone as the wallet), and it is exactly the case QR cannot serve. The typed
   code always works as the universal fallback (no camera, no push, accessibility-safe,
   cross-device and same-device alike) — which is why it ships first.

## Shape

### The pending request

New table (name illustrative) `pending_oauth_authorizations`:

- `request_id` (random, high-entropy — used in QR / handoff link / push payload)
- `user_code` (short, human-typeable, e.g. 8 chars grouped — the Netflix path; formatted
  distinctly from the agent claim code and the operator claim code; ADR-0026 already
  warns these "share a word, not a mechanism")
- client_id + resolved client metadata snapshot, requested scopes, PAR linkage
- requesting origin/IP/user-agent (for wallet display)
- optional `login_hint` DID (pre-bound account, if the client supplied one)
- status: `pending` / `approved` / `denied` / `expired`; granted-scope set on approval
- created/expires (~5 min), single-use

### Consent-page flow (`oauth_authorize.rs`, second path)

1. `GET /oauth/authorize` for a passwordless-capable flow renders the wallet path
   (alongside the password form while passworded accounts exist): creates the pending
   request, shows the `user_code`, an "Open in Obsign" handoff link carrying
   `request_id` (Phase A), and later a QR (Phase B).
2. The page observes `GET /oauth/authorize/status?request_id=…` (JS poll with the same
   `slow_down` throttling discipline as `claim_polling.rs`; no-JS fallback: an
   "I've approved — continue" button).
3. On `approved`, the page completes through the **existing** tail of
   `post_authorization`: scope reduction already decided, `store_authorization_code`,
   303 to `redirect_uri?code=…&state=…&iss=…`. The token endpoint (PKCE + DPoP) is
   untouched.

### Wallet approval

Reuses the agent-claim screen shape: enter code (or arrive via handoff/QR/push with
`request_id`) → **preview** (client name, origin, requesting IP/geo, scope list —
reusing the scope-preview treatment from `AgentClaimApprovalScreen.svelte`, and the
per-scope uncheck moves here: the wallet is the trusted UI for this path, so the granted
set is chosen in the wallet, not on the page) → biometric gate → sign → submit.

Approval credential: a **device-key-signed canonical envelope** in the
`sovereign_session.rs` mold — domain-versioned string binding server DID, account DID,
signing key, `request_id`, `client_id`, a hash of the granted scope set, timestamp,
nonce; verified against the **authoritative current PLC `rotationKeys`** (same
authoritative-fetch discipline, same nonce anti-replay pattern). This keeps consent
strictly key-sovereign: the thing that can approve a login is the thing that owns the
identity, sessions optional. (The alternative — authenticate the approval route with
`authenticate_account_owner` and skip the envelope — is less code but binds approval to
session state instead of the key; the envelope also gives per-approval non-repudiation
for the audit log.) Passkeys/WebAuthn remain the complementary *browser-native* factor
from the MM-312 open question — additive later, not a competitor to this path.

Account binding: if the request carries a `login_hint`, the approving wallet's DID must
match. Otherwise the approving wallet binds its DID at approval time (exactly like the
agent claim confirm), and the wallet screen states it explicitly: "Sign in to
**{client}** at **{origin}** as **@{handle}**".

### The push slot (Phase C, after MM-311)

Push adds only a delivery path: Custos seals `{type: "login-approval", request_id,
client_name, origin, code}` to the device (the relay design's exact payload), the wallet
deep-links into the same approval screen — with **number matching now mandatory**: the
consent page displays a 2-digit number for push-delivered prompts and the wallet requires
the user to enter/select it before the biometric gate, plus origin display. Nothing about
the primitive, the envelope, or the completion path changes.

## Suggested phasing

- **Phase A — code + handoff (no push, no camera).** The pending-request table/routes,
  the second consent-page path, typed `user_code` entry in the wallet (clone of the
  agent-claim screen), the same-device handoff link. Depends on nothing unbuilt.
  **Landed (2026-07-18):** `pending_oauth_authorizations` + `oauth_consent_audit_events`
  (V056), `crypto::encode_oauth_consent_envelope` (+ shared golden vector), the
  `routes/oauth_consent.rs` routes (wallet preview, `slow_down`-throttled status poll,
  device-key-signed approve/deny against authoritative PLC `rotationKeys`, browser
  completion through the existing code-issuance tail), the wallet path on the consent page,
  and the wallet's `oauth_consent.rs` IPC + `OAuthConsentApprovalScreen`. The signed
  envelope binds `request_id` + `client_id` + decision + granted-scope hash; single-use is
  enforced by the guarded status transitions (which, with the `request_id` binding, subsume
  a nonce store — no separate nonce table). Handoff link degrades to copy-the-code (the
  wallet has no deep-link handler yet, per ADR-0006).
- **Phase B — QR.** Encode `request_id` + origin on the consent page; wallet scan screen
  feeding the same approval flow. Camera plumbing is the only new work.
  **Landed (2026-07-19):** the consent page renders an inline-SVG QR (`qrcodegen` →
  `render_qr_svg` in `oauth_templates.rs`) encoding the wallet's private-use handoff URI
  (`org.obsign.identitywallet:/consent?request_id=…&origin=…`) beside the typed `user_code`, which
  stays rendered as the no-camera / accessibility fallback; the same URI backs both the QR and the
  same-device "Open in Obsign" link. The wallet gains a `preview_oauth_consent_by_request_id` IPC
  command (the server's preview endpoint already resolved by `request_id`) and a camera scan screen
  on `OAuthConsentApprovalScreen` via `@tauri-apps/plugin-barcode-scanner` (mobile-only, `#[cfg(mobile)]`,
  `NSCameraUsageDescription`, `barcode-scanner:default`). The scan path extracts **only** the
  `request_id` from the QR (`parseConsentQr`) and re-verifies it server-side — the client/origin/scope
  the wallet displays always come from the server's record, never the QR — then feeds the identical
  preview → biometric → device-key-signed-envelope flow. No server protocol change beyond encoding
  the QR payload.
- **Phase C — push + number matching.** After the notification relay (MM-311) lands:
  `login-approval` notification type, deep-link approve/deny, number-match UX.

Prerequisite note: the 2026-07-12 exploration named the Shamir **reconstruction**
ceremony a hard prerequisite for removing the password escape hatch; both reconstruction
ceremonies (escrow-assisted and sovereign) have since landed (`share_recovery.rs`;
[identity-and-key-custody.md](../architecture/identity-and-key-custody.md), verified
2026-07-18), so that gate is satisfied.

## Security invariants (all channels)

- Wallet approval screen always shows client name, origin/redirect host, requested
  scopes, and requesting IP/geo before the biometric gate; approval is impossible
  without the preview render.
- `user_code`/`request_id` single-use, ~5-minute expiry, rate-limited creation per
  client and per IP; status endpoint throttled like `claim_polling.rs`.
- The signed envelope binds the specific request (`request_id`, `client_id`, granted
  scope hash) — an approval cannot be replayed onto a different request or a widened
  scope set.
- Approval verification consults authoritative PLC state, never the cached DID doc
  (matching `sovereign_session.rs`).
- Denials and approvals both terminate the request; audit rows in the mold of
  `agent_audit`.

## Open questions

- **Same-device handoff mechanics on iOS.** ADR-0006 established that *server-initiated*
  redirects cannot launch the wallet from a browser context; a *user-tapped* universal
  link from inside another app's `ASWebAuthenticationSession`/`SFSafariViewController`
  is a different case but needs on-device validation. The typed code is the guaranteed
  fallback either way, so this only gates polish, not the phase.
- **Return-trip UX after same-device approval**: the user must app-switch back to the
  client app whose consent page then completes — acceptable (this is how bank-app
  confirmation flows feel) but worth prototyping.
- **Does the wallet-path consent page still render the password form?** Proposal:
  render the password form only for accounts that have one (requires the identifier
  first, or render both paths side by side as today's form does with checkboxes).
- **Number format for the Phase C match code**: 2-digit select-from-three (Microsoft
  style) vs type-the-number (GitHub style). Type-the-number is stronger against
  guess-taps; decide with the push UX.

# Obsign (identity-wallet) Mobile App

Last verified: 2026-07-08
Last updated: 2026-07-26

## Purpose

Tauri v2 iOS application — SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5 frontend running in a native WKWebView, communicating with a Rust backend exclusively through Tauri's IPC bridge.

## Browser test harness (drive the app without a simulator)

The whole frontend runs in a plain desktop browser under `vite dev` — the only thing the
browser lacks is the Tauri `invoke()` seam, which the harness intercepts with Tauri's
official `mockIPC`. This lets an agent (or a human) reach every screen and reproduce any
state, including rare error states, without a Mac/Xcode/simulator. Design + acceptance
criteria: [docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md](../../docs/archive/design-plans/2026-07-12-browser-harness.md).

**Start it** (or use the `.claude/launch.json` config `wallet-harness` / `wallet-harness-proxy`):
- **Fake mode** (default, no backend needed): `pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness` → http://localhost:5173.
- **Proxy mode** (real thin-HTTP calls against a hermetic local PDS): in one terminal
  `cargo build -p pds` then `just harness-pds` (prints the URL + admin token); in another,
  `VITE_HARNESS_PDS_URL=<url> VITE_HARNESS_ADMIN_TOKEN=<token> pnpm --dir apps/identity-wallet dev:harness:proxy`.
- Plain `pnpm dev` never activates the harness (double-gated on `import.meta.env.DEV && VITE_HARNESS`);
  `pnpm check:harness-absence` proves it is tree-shaken out of production builds.

**`window.__harness` console API** (both modes):
- `.scenario(name)` — switch preset and reload (persists across reload). Presets:
  `fresh-install`, `foreign-pds` (a spec-compliant non-Custos host — advertises no
  capabilities, so the create flow's gate closes and steers to import),
  `unreachable-pds` (the same empty capability list, but `reached: false` — the gate must
  show a retryable error, never the steer), `one-identity`, `multi-identity`,
  `alert-active`, `device-key-unusable` (a device restored from an encrypted backup: the
  device-key metadata came back, the Secure Enclave key did not — the only way to reach the
  "can no longer sign" degraded state in a browser with no enclave), `migration-in-flight`,
  `agent-connected`, `app-password-minted`, plus the share-recovery matrix:
  `recover-escrow` (happy path A — iCloud Share 1 + zero-delay escrow release),
  `recover-sovereign` (happy path B — manual Share 3 entry; paste
  `state().recovery.fixtures.share3Words` or `.share3`), `recover-wrong-set`
  (`fixtures.wrongSet` → SHARE_SET_MISMATCH), `recover-corrupt-share`
  (`fixtures.corrupt` → SHARE_CHECKSUM), `recover-mismatch` (verification fails —
  shares don't match the identity), `recover-pending-delay` (24h escrow window; the
  second poll releases), `recover-cancelled` (pending release cancelled → uniform
  401 on poll), `recover-epilogue-resume` (launch resumes an interrupted rotation
  epilogue); plus the escrow-less kit pair: `self-held-kit` (a claimed identity on a
  non-Custos host — device key at `rotationKeys[0]`, a longer claimed tail than the
  re-key's `[device, PDS]`, no recovery key, host advertises nothing) and
  `self-held-kit-escrow-host` (the same identity after the kit, now hosted somewhere that
  DOES advertise `escrow` — the upsell seam's only true state). `.scenarios` lists them.
- `.failNext(command, error)` — make the next call of `command` reject with a typed error,
  e.g. `window.__harness.failNext('create_account', { code: 'EXPIRED_CODE' })`.
- `.emit(event, payload)` — deliver a Tauri event to live `listen()` subscribers;
  `window.__harness.emit('auth_ready')` simulates the OAuth deep-link return.
- `.state()` — a read-only snapshot of the fake store. `.mode` is `'fake'` or `'proxy'`.

**Proxy mode is real only for the thin-HTTP subset** — `create_account` (mints + redeems a
real claim code, POSTs `/v1/accounts/mobile`) and `get_available_user_domains`
(describeServer). By the honest boundary, these stay **faked even in proxy mode** (heavy
Rust logic with no thin-HTTP form): the DID ceremony (`perform_did_ceremony`,
`*_did_web_ceremony`), OAuth completion (`prepare/complete_oauth_flow`), the migration
transfer legs (`transfer_repo`/`transfer_blobs`/…, `finalize_migration`), recovery/claim
PLC ops, and the agent surfaces (which need a real post-ceremony session the faked
ceremony never mints). Fidelity the browser can never cover: real Keychain/Secure-Enclave,
the biometric prompt, ASWebAuthenticationSession, WKWebView rendering, safe-area insets,
camera/QR — those stay simulator/device concerns.

**Fake handler coverage is enforced:** every command in `$lib/ipc` must have a handler in
`src/lib/harness/registry.ts` or `registry.test.ts` fails (`pnpm test`). Harness code lives
in `src/lib/harness/` (`install`/`registry`/`state`/`scenarios`/`control` + `proxy/`),
activated by `src/hooks.client.ts`.

## Contracts

### Frontend (SvelteKit 2 + Svelte 5)

**Exposes:**
- `src/lib/ipc/` — per-domain typed wrappers for all Tauri IPC commands, re-exported from `src/lib/ipc/index.ts`; import from `$lib/ipc` instead of calling `invoke()` directly. Exports: `createAccount()`, `performDIDCeremony()`, `registerHandle()`, `getAvailableUserDomains()`, `registerCreatedIdentity()`, `startOAuthFlow()`, `getPdsUrl()`, `savePdsUrl()`, `getPdsCapabilities()`/`hasPdsCapability()`, `getAppearancePreference()`, `setAppearancePreference()`, `resolveIdentity()`, `authenticateSourcePds()`, `requestClaimVerification()`, `signAndVerifyClaim()`, `submitClaim()`, `listIdentities()`, `getStoredDidDoc()`, `getDeviceKeyId()`, `checkIdentityStatus()`, `buildRecoveryOverride()`, `submitRecoveryOverride()`, and their associated types (`CreateAccountResult`, `CreateAccountError`, `DIDCeremonyResult`, `DIDCeremonyError`, `RegisterHandleResult`, `RegisterHandleError`, `RegisterIdentityError`, `OAuthError`, `PdsConfigError`, `AppearancePreference`, `AppearanceError`, `IdentityInfo`, `VerifiedClaimOp`, `OpDiff`, `ServiceChange`, `ClaimResult`, `ResolveError`, `ClaimError`, `IdentityStoreError`, `UnauthorizedChange`, `IdentityStatus`, `SignedRecoveryOp`, `RecoveryError`, `SignedMigrationOp`, `MigrateError`) and migration wrappers (`buildMigrationOp()`, `submitMigrationOp()`) and the did:web wrappers (`prepareDidWebCeremony()`/`completeDidWebCeremony()` — the create-flow did:web ceremony, returning `DidWebPreparation`/`DIDCeremonyResult`; `importDidWebIdentity()` — bring an existing did:web under wallet management, returning `ImportedDidWebIdentity`, error `ImportDidWebError`; `buildDidWebMigrationDocument()`/`submitDidWebMigrationDocument()` — compose + publish-verify the did:web outbound-migration identity leg, type `DidWebMigrationDocument`) and outbound-migration orchestrator wrappers (`prepareMigration()`, `authenticateMigrationSource()`, `PreparedMigration`, `MigrationError`, `BlobLoss`, `BlobTransferDirection`), the sovereign change-handle wrappers (`getIdentityHandleDomains()`, `changeHandle()` — biometric-gated) with type `HandleChangeError`, and the unlock wrappers (`getIdentityUnlockRoute()`, `unlockIdentityWithPassword()`) with types (`UnlockRoute`, `UnlockMethod`, `UnlockError`), and and identity-removal wrappers (`requestIdentityRemoval()`, `confirmIdentityRemoval()`, `tombstoneIdentity()`, `listPendingRemovals()`, `forgetIdentityLocally()`) with types (`RemovalError`, `RemovalOutcome`), and the share-recovery wrappers (`startShareRecovery()`, `addRecoveryShare()`, `removeRecoveryShare()`, `initiateEscrowRelease()`, `requestEscrowRelease()`, `verifyRecoveryShares()`, `recoverIdentity()` — biometric-gated, `runRecoveryEpilogue()`, `getPendingRecoveryEpilogue()`, `confirmRecoveryBackup()`) with types (`ShareRecoveryError`, `CollectedShare`, `RecoveryTarget`, `EscrowReleaseStatus`, `RecoveredIdentity`, `RecoveryAnchor`, `EpilogueResult`, `PendingEpilogue`), and the media-backup wrappers (`getBlobBackupStatus()`, `setBlobBackupEnabled()`, `runBlobBackup()`, `restoreBlobBackup()` — biometric-gated, and the app-global background-sweep settings `getBackgroundBackupSettings()` / `setBackgroundBackupSettings()`) with types (`BlobBackupStatus`, `BlobBackupRunReport`, `BlobRestoreReport`, `BlobFailure`, `BackupLocation`, `BlobBackupError`, `BackgroundBackupSettings`, `BackgroundBackupError`), and the repo-backup wrappers (`getRepoBackupStatus()`, `setRepoBackupEnabled()`, `runRepoBackup()`, `exportRepoBackup()` — none biometric-gated; all read the public `getRepo` or local disk) with types (`RepoBackupStatus`, `RepoBackupRunReport`, `RepoExport`, `RepoBackupError`)
- `src/lib/components/onboarding/` — one screen component per step of the create / import / recover onboarding flows (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory; hand-counted lists here drifted twice)
- `src/lib/components/home/` — the home-surface screen components (the directory listing is the authoritative inventory) plus the DIDAvatar utility component (deterministic DID-derived hue circle). **ProtectionScreen is the app-level Defend surface** (the `protection` step), opened from the home list's protection strip — which is a **door, not a readout**: the PLC monitor runs unattended and, before this surface existed, produced nothing a user could look at, so the wallet's central trust claim rested on an assertion. It opens with a `StatusPanel` over the whole wallet, then every identity's status row (ordered most-severe-first by `$lib/protection`; an alarmed row taps straight through to `alert_detail`, every other row to the identity panel), then the monitor history — the sweep log from `getMonitorHistory`, with a "Check now" action whose result lands in that log. The strip and the panel render the SAME `summarize()` output, so the door can never state something the room contradicts, and `identityReturnStep` (the tier-up sibling of `alertReturnStep`) keeps Back from ejecting someone working the list. **IdentityScreen is the per-identity instrument panel** (the `identity_detail` step) and the spine of the home-surface IA: state leads, actions follow. It opens with a `StatusPanel` derived from `$lib/identity-status`, then a **Use** zone (sign in to an app / sign in to Bluesky / my agents), then two doors — **MoveOrRebuildScreen** (`move_or_rebuild`: outbound migration + sovereign disaster recovery, an exit kept findable rather than filed under maintenance) and **ManageIdentityScreen** (`manage_identity`: change handle, backups, DID document, plus an Advanced entry). **AdvancedToolsScreen** (`advanced_tools`) is the vestibule: a plain-language framing card stating what protocol-level tools do, then the surgery list (add a recovery key, rotate repo signing key, repair hosting endpoint, remove identity). The vestibule is **additive framing only** — every operation keeps its own biometric gate, pre-sign review, and hold-to-confirm. SecurityCheckup is the quiet disclosure hanging off a secure StatusPanel (key custody, public-record watch, media + posts backup freshness), all reads of state the wallet already holds. ChangeHandleScreen is the sovereign change-handle surface reached from ManageIdentityScreen's "Change handle" row (did:plc + device-key-as-root only): it loads the hosting PDS's served domains, pre-flights the session (`ensureIdentitySession`, `unlockIdentity` on `NEEDS_UNLOCK`), then runs the biometric-gated `changeHandle`. AppPasswordsScreen is the app-password surface reached from the identity screen's Use zone ("Sign in to Bluesky"): it lists/mints/revokes the account's scoped app passwords via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (SESSION_LOCKED → `unlockIdentity` + retry ($lib/unlock: sovereign login on a Custos host, password prompt elsewhere); mint and revoke are biometric-gated; the generated secret is shown once with copy and never persisted). MediaBackupScreen is the user-held blob-backup surface reached from ManageIdentityScreen's "Backups" row (media and posts are presented as one item because they are one job): opt-in with the mirror size always shown, "Back up now" (incremental, CID-verified sync pass over public sync endpoints — no session), and a biometric-gated "Restore to server" (`uploadBlob` via `SessionProvider::full_access_client`; SESSION_LOCKED → `unlockIdentity` + retry ($lib/unlock: sovereign login on a Custos host, password prompt elsewhere)), with per-blob failures listed rather than aborting the run. The same screen also holds a "Back up your posts" section (`repo_backup.rs`): opt-in with the snapshot size + last-backup shown, and "Back up posts now" (a full-CAR `getRepo` snapshot, validated client-side before it replaces the prior copy — no session, no biometric); there is no repo "restore" button (an `importRepo` needs a deactivated account, so restore flows through migration). `+page.svelte` fires silent opportunistic `runBlobBackup` **and** `runRepoBackup` passes on app open for opted-in identities (each on its own per-DID flag). MyAgentsScreen is the agent list; AgentDetailScreen is the per-agent sub-view (audit-trail paging + biometric-gated revoke) it renders on selection, its lifetime scoped to that selection. RemoveIdentityScreen is the permanent-removal flow (warn → emailed-code + password → biometric-gated hold-to-remove → progress, with a "tombstone pending, retry" state), reached from AdvancedToolsScreen's destructive `onremove` (behind the vestibule) — offered for **both** DID methods, with the screen branching on `did:web:` throughout: the warning drops the "retire on the network by tombstoning" promise (a did:web has no tombstone), the escape hatch's advanced "also retire on the network" option is withheld (it could not do what it says), and a successful removal ends in the `web_epilogue` state rather than returning to the identity list — the DID keeps resolving until its `did.json` leaves the domain, which only whoever controls that domain can do. The screen switches on the outcome's `tombstoneCid` being null (the backend's honest report that no tombstone was published), not on the DID string alone

The localStorage mirror (key `appearance-preference`) exists only so `src/app.html`'s inline `<head>` script can apply a forced appearance before first paint; the Keychain is the source of truth

Tested by `agent-scopes.test.ts`

Thresholds: expired = 0, critical < 4h, warning < 24h, safe >= 24h
- `src/routes/+page.svelte` — root page: three-flow state machine starting at `mode_select` (whose `oncreate` opens `identity_method`, `IdentityMethodScreen` — the did:plc / did:web method fork). **Create flow:** mode_select -> `identity_method` -> [did:plc: pds_config; new did:web: `did_web_path` -> `did_web_domain` -> pds_config] -> claim_code -> email -> handle -> password (every pre-submit step wires `onback` to the previous step) -> loading -> did_ceremony (the did:web branch runs `did_web_ceremony` instead) -> did_success -> shamir_backup -> handle_registration -> complete -> authenticating -> home (after handle_registration succeeds, `finishCreateFlow()` calls `registerCreatedIdentity()` to persist the new identity to `IdentityStore` so it appears in `IdentityListHome` — best-effort, never blocks the flow). `pds_config` is a **capability gate**, not just a form: after `savePdsUrl` (which re-probes the host, so this reads a warm cache) it calls `getPdsCapabilities()` and, unless the host advertises `createCeremony`, routes to `create_unavailable` (`CreateUnavailableScreen`) instead of `claim_code` — the create ceremony is Custos-structural, so a standard PDS is refused before the user types an account detail rather than failing inside `/v1/accounts/mobile`. This is the one gate that reads `ServerCapabilities.reached`: it does not merely withhold a feature, it tells the user their server cannot create identities, and a host that could not be asked must produce a retryable error instead of that accusation. The gate covers both create paths, since the did:web branch also passes through `pds_config`. From `create_unavailable` the import flow is one tap away with the chosen server still configured. **Import flow:** mode_select -> identity_input -> pds_auth -> email_verification -> review_operation -> claim_success -> home. **Existing did:web** takes the third `identity_method` branch: `did_web_path` (choose "existing") -> `did_web_existing`, which calls `importDidWebIdentity()` to bring the live document under wallet management, then enters the method-agnostic outbound-migration flow at `migration_start` (a did:web has no claim ceremony — control is proven by the domain publish and the source-PDS password, not a PLC op). **Home:** home -> { protection (the app-level Defend surface, from the protection strip) | identity_detail (the instrument panel) -> { move_or_rebuild -> { migration_start | recovery_rebuild_start } | manage_identity -> { change_handle | media_backup | did_document | advanced_tools -> { self_held_kit_review | rotate_repo_key | endpoint_repair | remove_identity } } | app_passwords | my_agents | oauth_consent_approval | alert_detail -> recovery_override } }, with `protection` itself reaching `identity_detail` and `alert_detail`. Each re-homed screen's `onback` returns to the door it now hangs off, which is the only spatial model this flat step union has. Two surfaces are reachable from more than one place, so each records where it came from rather than assuming: `alert_detail` (home's card strip, the identity panel's critical status, or a Protection row) via `alertReturnStep`, and `identity_detail` (the home list or a Protection row) via `identityReturnStep`. A fixed back path would eject the user out of the identity they were standing in, or out of the list they were working through. On mount, checks for existing identities via `listIdentities()` and skips to `home` if any exist. Registers a `visibilitychange` listener that calls `checkIdentityStatus()` when the app returns to foreground while on the `home` **or** `protection` step — Protection's whole subject is how fresh the reading is, so it is the worst place to sit showing a stale one

Distinct terminal errors, never looped: `NeedsUnlock{reason}`, `RateLimited{retryAfter}`, `UnsupportedHost`, `Offline{message}`, `ServerFailure{status}`, `Keychain`, `InvalidResponse`. A revoked refresh (400/401) and a host change both delete the dead record; a rate limit keeps it. Coalescing is a re-read (not a shared future): the second caller for one DID waits on the lock, then re-loads the freshly-persisted record — so a refresh token can never be raced into replay detection. Does NOT reuse `OAuthClient::refresh_token_bearer` (which is in-memory-only by design) — the provider owns refresh+persist. Module-level XRPC functions (take `&OAuthClient`): the claim helpers `request_plc_operation_signature(client)`, `sign_plc_operation(client, request)`, `get_recommended_did_credentials(client)`; and the outbound-migration helpers `get_service_auth(client, aud, lxm)`, `create_account_migration(client, request)` (maps HTTP 409 → `PdsClientError::DidAlreadyExists` for resume), `import_repo(client, car_bytes)`, `upload_blob(client, mime, bytes)`, `list_missing_blobs(client, cursor)`, `get_preferences(client)`, `put_preferences(client, prefs)`, `check_account_status(client)`, `activate_account(client)`, `deactivate_account(client)`. Every authenticated XRPC helper routes its non-2xx branch through the private `classify_xrpc_response(context, resp)` (→ pure `classify_xrpc_error(status, retry_after, body)`), so a server response is classified by status — `429 → RateLimited{retry_after}`, `401 → Unauthorized`, else `XrpcError{status, error, message}` carrying the atproto error envelope — instead of being flattened into `NetworkError`. `NetworkError` is now transport-only. Types: `PlcDidDocument` (Clone), `PlcService` (Clone), `AuthServerMetadata`, `PdsParResponse`, `SignPlcOperationRequest`, `SignPlcOperationResponse`, `RecommendedCredentials`, plus migration types `DescribeServerResponse`, `ServiceAuthToken`, `CreateAccountMigrationRequest`, `CreateAccountResponse`, `CreateSessionResponse`, `MissingBlob`/`MissingBlobs`, `UploadBlobResponse`, `AccountStatus` (from `checkAccountStatus`). `PdsClientError` enum: HANDLE_NOT_FOUND, DID_NOT_FOUND, PDS_UNREACHABLE, NETWORK_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, UNAUTHORIZED, XRPC_ERROR, INVALID_RESPONSE, OAUTH_FAILED, DID_ALREADY_EXISTS, INVALID_CREDENTIALS, AUTH_FACTOR_TOKEN_REQUIRED, INSECURE_PDS_URL (serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`)
- `src/plc_monitor.rs` — PLC monitoring module: `PlcMonitor` (borrows `PdsClient`; `check_all()` iterates the managed DIDs that have a PLC audit log — `is_monitorable`, i.e. `did:plc:` only — and `check_for_changes(did)` diffs current audit log against cached log and classifies new entries as authorized/unauthorized by verifying signatures against the device key); `run_monitoring_loop(app_handle)` (spawned once at app startup, checks every 15 minutes via `tokio::time::interval` with `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`, emits `"plc_alert"` Tauri event to frontend when unauthorized changes detected); `check_identity_status` (Tauri IPC command: synchronous foreground check over the same monitorable set, returns `Vec<IdentityStatus>`). Types: `UnauthorizedChange` { cid, created_at, signing_key, operation } (camelCase serialization), `IdentityStatus` { did, check_failed, unauthorized_changes } (camelCase serialization), `MonitorError` { NetworkError, IdentityStoreError, ParseError } (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE tag serialization). **Sweep history** — the monitor's user-visible record of its own work, the evidence behind the Protection surface: a completed pass (from either the background timer or `check_identity_status`) is folded into the global `monitor-history` Keychain record by the pure, tested `fold_sweep`, and read back by the synchronous `get_monitor_history` command. Types: `SweepTrigger` (`background` | `foreground`), `SweepRecord` { at, trigger, identities_checked, identities_failed, unauthorized_found }, `IdentityLastChecked` { did, last_verified_at }, `MonitorHistory` { sweeps (newest first, capped at 20), identities, interval_secs }. Every count is about identities the monitor actually looked at, since `check_all` omits anything `is_monitorable` rejects — a did:web is not a checked identity nor a failed one, and never appears in `identities`. Three further rules keep the log honest: a **failed** check leaves an identity's previous `last_verified_at` standing (the last verification is still a fact); only identities present in the sweep survive the fold (a removed DID leaves the log on the next pass, and the record can never resurrect one); and identical *foreground* passes within five minutes coalesce, so ordinary navigation — which fires a check on launch, on foreground, and on entering the identity screen — cannot evict the background sweeps the log exists to evidence. Reads are **fail-open** (a corrupt record reads as an empty log), the deliberate inverse of `ceremony-staging`'s fail-closed contract: this record holds counts and timestamps, so erroring on it would cost the user the sweep running now to preserve a readout of sweeps already past

This replaces the previous auth on the never-refreshed global `"session-token"`, whose lapse dead-ended every agent command as a bogus connection error. Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&OAuthClient`, tested against httpmock. `AgentsError` (NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CODE_NOT_FOUND, CODE_EXPIRED, ALREADY_CLAIMED, ACCESS_DENIED, AGENT_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, SESSION_LOCKED, NETWORK_ERROR, UNKNOWN) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }`; the ceremony's `{error}` codes map onto it in `map_ceremony_error`, and a session-lifecycle failure via `map_session_error` (only a genuine transport failure is NETWORK_ERROR — a NeedsUnlock is SESSION_LOCKED, every other verdict is UNKNOWN), so denial/expiry/lock render as explicit states

Request cores are `_impl` functions taking `&PdsClient`, tested against httpmock. `ConsentError` (IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED_HOST, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND, APPROVAL_REJECTED, ALREADY_RESOLVED, RATE_LIMITED, TRANSPORT_FAILURE, KEYCHAIN_FAILURE, SIGNING_FAILED, DID_MISMATCH, SERVER_MISMATCH, INVALID_RESPONSE, SERVER_FAILURE) serialized as `{ code: "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE" }` with camelCase fields

All three resolve a per-DID full-access session via `SessionProvider::full_access_client` (the PDS routes require full access — an app password cannot manage app passwords); a `NeedsUnlock` maps to `SESSION_LOCKED{reason}`, the frontend's cue to run `unlockIdentity(did)` and retry, mirroring `handle_change.rs`. Thin XRPC wrappers + response types (`AppPasswordCreated`, `AppPasswordEntry`) live in `pds_client.rs`; a 409 duplicate name maps to `DUPLICATE_NAME`. `AppPasswordsError` (SESSION_LOCKED, RATE_LIMITED, DUPLICATE_NAME, IDENTITY_NOT_FOUND, SERVER_ERROR, NETWORK_ERROR)
